errors.text_span: процента на нетните вноски на енергия спрямо наличното налично енергийно количество
errors.evidence: The phrase "наличното налично енергийно количество" (the available available energy quantity) is redundant and an awkward translation of "gross available energy" from the chart's subtitle.
The chart displays data for 40 distinct entities (EU-27 plus 39 other countries and regions), not 28.
The countries on the x-axis are not sorted alphabetically. For the most part, they are sorted in descending order of their 2018 energy dependency rate.

errors.text_span: EU-27, Malta, Luxembourg, Belgium, Spain, Ireland, Portugal, Lithuania, Greece, Austria, Germany, Netherlands, Slovenia, Croatia, Poland, Finland, Czechia, Bulgaria, Denmark, Sweden, France, Norway, United Kingdom, Iceland, Estonia, Serbia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Georgia и Молдова
errors.evidence: This list of countries presented in the description is incomplete; it omits Cyprus, Italy, Slovakia, Hungary, Latvia, Romania, Turkey, Albania, and Ukraine, all of which are present in the chart.
The y-axis scale includes negative values, extending down to -25%, and some data points (e.g., Denmark, Norway) have negative values.

errors.text_span: Най-ниската стълба за 2008 г. е за Албания
errors.evidence: This is incorrect. The lowest value in 2008 belongs to Norway (-564.5). The lowest visible value is for Denmark (approx. -25%). Albania's value for 2008 is positive (around 50%).
The bar for Albania in 2008 reaches approximately 50%, not 10%.

errors.text_span: а най-високата - за Косово с около 80%
errors.evidence: The description hallucinates this data point for 2008. According to a footnote in the chart, data for Kosovo for 2008 is not available, and no bar is shown.
The value for Albania in 2018 is approximately 30%, not 12%.
The value for Kosovo in 2018 is approximately 25%, not 82%.
The bars representing the year 2018 are pink/magenta, not green.
The description fails to mention the grouped structure of the bar chart, where for each country, there are two bars representing the years 2008 and 2018.

The description omits any mention of the footnotes, which provide critical information about the cut bars for Norway and their actual values, as well as the missing data for certain countries in 2008.
